issues.text: The lesson says the notifications row 'is not part of the order' and that every arrow crossing a boundary is an id, but at stage-2 `Notification` holds `public Order? Order { get; set; }`, QueuedNotifier sets `Order = order`, and the email job reaches the customer through `notification.Order!.Customer!`. A reader sent 'further down the file' (s5) meets this object reference right after Payment, with no explanation.
issues.quote: That row is not part of the order: `NotificationSender` later claims, sends and updates it on its own.
issues.fix: Append to that sentence: "(`Notification` does keep an `Order` navigation: `QueuedNotifier` sets it so EF Core fills in `order_id`, and the email job reads through it; nothing changes an order through it.)"
